title: Hang a weight on a spring hook without shock-loading it
instruction: Hang the grey weight on the hook by its ring and let go.
context: A load hung on a spring scale or spring balancer must be lowered until the scale carries it before it is let go; letting go on first contact makes the spring overshoot toward twice the load and drives the scale's maximum-reading pointer into its overload range. Unlike TK-34GDSF (read a spring at rest) and TK-ES7KZB (let a loaded spring rise slowly), this task scores the peak load the robot puts on a compliant support while handing a load to it.
setup: Station table, top 0.7475 m. World frame: x away from the robot, y to its left, origin between the arm bases (y = ±0.305 m). Fixed hanging spring scale (steel stand): dark base plate 120 × 120 × 10 mm centred at (0.38, 0.019); grey post 30 (x) × 78 (y) × 190 mm on it, front face at x = 0.365. On the front face, a dark steel carriage 8 (x) × 34 (y) × 40 mm (z), centred at y = 0, slides down against a 150 N/m spring (damping 0.6 N·s/m, 70 mm travel). It carries the hook: a square steel pin 10 × 10 mm, 60 mm long, pointing at the robot from x = 0.357 to 0.297, its top face about 169 mm above the table at rest, with a 5 × 10 × 6 mm upturned tip at its free end; the carriage spans 25 mm below to 15 mm above the pin's top face. Beside the carriage (y 0.020–0.035) is a yellow painted-steel drag pointer 5 × 15 × 8 mm standing 5 mm off the post face, its top edge 180 mm above the table at the start; the hook pushes it down and it stays at the hook's largest stretch. Next to it (y 0.040–0.055) a printed scale strip 15 mm wide standing 3 mm off the face: white for the first 37 mm below the pointer's start, red from 37 to 75 mm. Loose weight, 0.4 kg: grey aluminium body 50 × 50 × 60 mm with a dark rigid steel ring on top (5 × 5 mm bars, opening 30 mm wide × 28 mm high, facing the post), standing on the table at (0.25, 0.12). The weight alone stretches the hook 26 mm.
scoring: Read from the photo and the video. The weight counts as hung when the pin passes through its ring (between the tip and the carriage), its bottom is at least 2 cm above the table, the hook carries the whole weight (it is stretched within 2 mm of its static value, 26.2 mm, so 24.2–28.2 mm below its unloaded position: the weight's full load to within 0.3 N), and the weight has shown no visible motion over the last 1.5 s. 1.0: hung, and the drag pointer's top edge never reached the red band (the hook's largest stretch over the whole trial stayed under 37 mm). 0: anything else, including hung but with the pointer in the red band (the hook stretched 37 mm or more at some point; an overloaded scale is taken out of service), the weight still in the gripper, on the table, resting on top of the pin without the ring around it, or hanging in front of the tip.
fidelity: Rigid boxes. The stand is a hanging spring scale: a 150 N/m damped spring slider with 70 mm travel (a 1 kg tubular lab spring scale is about 125 N/m with about 80 mm travel), a maximum-reading (drag) pointer, and a red overload range from 37 mm (1.4 times the weight's stretch). In the simulator the pointer is moved to the largest stretch sampled at 20 Hz, so it can read 2-3 mm under the true peak. The weight's ring is fixed to its body.
reset_notes: Push the drag pointer back to its start (the top of the white band) and stand the weight back at its start. Nothing is consumed.
